findings.title: The two blink-phase screenshots are not guaranteed to land in different phases
findings.claim: Task 3 gets its 'one shot per blink phase' by launching Electron twice, with extra delays of 0 and 250 ms. Each capture happens at (navigation to shotReady) + 2500 + extra ms on the page's own performance.now(). The load time differs from launch to launch, and the 2 Hz damage blink holds each phase for only 250 ms, so the 250 ms offset does not fix the phase. About half the time both shots will show the same phase, and the spec's pass/fail check then cannot be done.
findings.evidence: plan L388-L389, L392-L393 (the 0/250 ms pairs), L396 ('250 ms apart lands the 2 Hz damage blink in the other phase'), L405 (the per-phase check); crt-map plan L2346-L2348 (wait for shotReady, then 2500 + extra); scene.ts:L99 (layer.draw(..., performance.now() / 1000)); crtTheme.ts:L14-L18 (DAMAGE_BLINK_HZ = 2, blink = floor(t*4) % 2, so each phase lasts 0.25 s)
findings.why: The spec's screenshot check (spec L132) has to see both phases at zoom 0.5 and at 1.2. With random phases, the subagent either reports a false failure or compares two shots of the same phase and calls it a pass.
findings.fix: Pin the phase in the page. In main.ts, before createRenderer, add: `const ph = q.get('phase'); if (ph) { const real = performance.now.bind(performance); performance.now = () => { const r = real(); return r - (r % 500) + (ph === 'b' ? 260 : 10); }; }`. Use `&phase=a` / `&phase=b` in the shot list in place of the 0/250 extra delays (this holds the damage blink; the 1 Hz enemy ring then changes only every 0.5 s). Alternatively, in Step 4, require the subagent to confirm that the crew's level-2 room is a cut-out in one shot and solid in the other, and to retake the b shot if it is not.

findings.title: Running the CRT Step 4 'exactly' writes the shots into the CRT map's gate folder; the runner has no output folder to replace
findings.claim: Step 2 item 3 says to replace 'the output folder' in the runner. all.mjs has no such constant: it takes the folder as argv (crt-map plan L2366). The folder is set by `OUT="C:/Users/djuar/FTLite-shots/crt-map"` in the CRT Step 4 bash, which also copies three CRT reference images into crt-map. Step 3 says to run 'exactly as the CRT plan's Task 7 Step 4 says', so the shots go to FTLite-shots/crt-map, the folder of the CRT map's still-open owner look gate. Step 4 then reads from hull-silhouettes and finds nothing. The CRT Step 6 cleanup filter `*crt-map*shot.cjs*` also does not match this worktree.
findings.evidence: plan L396, L401; crt-map plan L2366 (outDir from argv), L2396-L2399 (OUT=crt-map, cp refs), L2428 (stop filter '*crt-map*shot.cjs*')
findings.why: A fresh subagent following the text verbatim writes into the wrong folder and adds files to another feature's gate folder. It is also left without a concrete stop command.
findings.fix: Write the Step 3 commands out in full: the port check; `npx vite --config .art/shots/vite.config.mjs` in the background; `E=node_modules/electron/dist/electron.exe; [ -f "$E" ] || E=/c/Users/djuar/FTLite/node_modules/electron/dist/electron.exe; rm -f .art/shots/shot.log; node .art/shots/all.mjs "$E" "C:/Users/djuar/FTLite-shots/hull-silhouettes"; grep -v wrote .art/shots/shot.log` (no cp); the seven expected `ok` lines; and the CRT Step 6 stop command with the filter `*hull-silhouettes*shot.cjs*`. Drop 'build', since the harness serves source through vite. Remove 'the output folder' from item 3.

findings.title: The harness's interiorCamera is left to be worked out at execution
findings.claim: Step 2 item 2 tells the subagent to read scene.ts and 'add any missing required field ... report what you added'. On today's branch the field and its constructor are known: DuelViewSource.interiorCamera is required, and the runtime builds it with createInteriorCamera(). Vite/esbuild does not type-check and scene.ts uses the field only for the interior view, which no shot covers, so this is harmless at runtime. It is still an open item a verbatim executor has to resolve.
findings.evidence: plan L385; scene.ts:L35 (readonly interiorCamera: InteriorCamera), scene.ts:L91 (used only when view === 'interior'); runtime.ts:L227 (createInteriorCamera()); render/duel/interiorCamera.ts:L28
findings.why: The brief treats 'check at execution' as a defect, and naming the field costs one line.
findings.fix: Replace item 2 with: add `import { createInteriorCamera } from '../../src/renderer/src/render/duel/interiorCamera';` and the field `interiorCamera: createInteriorCamera(),` in the `source` object after `cameras`.

findings.title: Small inaccuracies in Task 1's Interfaces and Task 2 Step 1's expected RED output
findings.claim: Task 1's Interfaces lists `hatchSegments` as consumed by the test, but the test imports only isConvex. Task 2 Step 1 expects tsc to report `hull` 'missing on ShipDraw in crtColours'. Before Step 2, the fixtures add `hull`, so tsc reports an excess property ('hull' does not exist in type 'ShipDraw' / Partial<ShipDraw>). vitest itself does not type-check, so the expected tsc error only appears if `npx tsc -b` is run at that step, and the step does not say to run it.
findings.evidence: plan L60 vs L69; plan L297; tests/crtColours.test.ts:L14, L23
findings.why: A literal-minded executor may stop because the observed RED output does not match the stated one.
findings.fix: Drop hatchSegments from L60. At L297, say: run `npx tsc -b`; expected: errors that 'hull' does not exist in type ShipDraw in tests/crtColours.test.ts; and vitest fails the two new tacticalModel assertions and the duelWeaponsView lock test (roomCentre('scout', 0).f = 0.67, not the wedge's 0.633).
